facts.fact: Madagascar Customs says Sydonia++ is its automated customs system, installed centrally, and that TradeNet electronically registers declarations and is operational at 11 offices, near-total coverage of clearance operations.
Madagascar Customs says paperless clearance, using a Midac web application alongside Sydonia, is under test at the Mamory Ivato office.

Madagascar Customs says TradeNet interconnects declarants, customs, banks and the ministries and control agencies that issue permits and licences for clearance, reinforcing the existing single window.

Ministerial arrete 36657/2015 requires all clearance exchanges at computerised customs offices to be transmitted electronically through the customs system, comprising SYDONIA and the TradeNet platform.

The Customs Code (art. 87, as amended by the 2023 finance law) requires declarations at customs offices equipped with computer systems to be lodged electronically, and art. 88 refers to an automated clearance system.
Madagascar's Customs Directorate clears goods on Sydonia World, described as the current clearance platform, and launched a pilot to improve its electronic clearance system.

The Ministry of Economy and Finance says the customs directorate and the Korea Customs Service officially launched on 4 December 2024 a project to modernise the electronic customs clearance system, with a data warehouse and full deployment expected in 2026.

facts.fact: Madagascar's customs administration says it analyses millions of records from SYDONIA, its customs management platform, and that automated controls have reduced clearance times.
GasyNet's chief executive says the TradeNet electronic single window, with its Douar customs module, is in service and has cut average clearance time to three days.
GasyNet's chief executive says TradeNet connects customs (Douar), control ministries and agencies (Midac) and shipping lines (Delivery Order) in one electronic single window.
